display.title: Episode 146: The Lost Letter, Chapter 1 (Chol HaMoed Sukkos)
display.summary_short: On Chol HaMoed Sukkos, Uncle Yossi explains why Sukkos is the 'time of our joy' and why the Torah dances with us at Hakafos, and begins the story of a rich Chassid who needed no blessing.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Chol HaMoed Sukkos. Uncle Yossi explains why Sukkos alone is called the 'time of our joy': we rejoice that we have a Jewish soul, that we have the Torah, and that we have Hashem, the one and only G-d. In place of the march, listeners learn and sing 'I Love Hashem.' Story time begins 'The Lost Letter': at his bedside in his last days, the Baal Shem Tov blesses his students one by one. Reb Leibel, the richest of them, healthy, generous and blessed with a large family, decides he needs no brachah, forgetting that fortune can turn. After a boy from the Tzivos Hashem Club leads the Shema, the story continues: the Baal Shem Tov asks Reb Leibel to deliver a sealed letter to a man named Reb Sholom. Arriving home soaked from a storm, Reb Leibel bends to remove his muddy boots, and the letter slips under a wooden closet. He forgets all about it. To be continued. Uncle Yossi then explains Hakafos on Simchas Torah: we celebrate finishing the Torah and starting again, and the Torah 'borrows' our feet, hands and voice to dance with us. The show closes with the Shofar Gadol contest ending next week and a refuah shleimah update.
display.lesson: However blessed we are, we always need Hashem's blessings; and on Simchas Torah we lend the Torah our feet, hands and voice so it can rejoice with us.

date.note: On air: 'right in the middle of Sukkos'; the contest ends 'till after Sukkos, that is, till next Tuesday, October the 23rd'. So this Tuesday is 16 Oct 1984 (Chol HaMoed).
